Subject: Redwood long-context eval — post-call recap + deliverables

Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery / evaluation planning call: 

Call summary:
- Primary use case: legal contract ingestion (20–30k average doc length) + multi-document summarization for legal ops.
- Key constraints: high-fidelity summaries, minimal truncation/semantic loss, and predictable per-token costs at scale.
- Existing infra: on AWS, S3 storage, interested in VPC/private deployment for sensitive PII.

Redwood recommended starting point (model fit):
- redwood-long-32k (primary): optimized for >32k context with prefix/KV caching — best balance of summary fidelity + latency.
- redwood-quant-64k-candidate (variant): higher effective context using quantization, good for batch offline summarization.
- fallback: redwood-8k-llama-compat for low-cost, low-latency routes where truncation risk is acceptable.

Eval artifacts we will share (attached / links):
- acme-long-context-eval-results-summary.pdf — executive summary and key failure modes.
- prompt-sets-v1.jsonl — the prompt set and positive / negative examples we ran.
- benchmark dashboard link: https://bench.redwood.ai/dashboards/acme-long-context

Key technical notes we discussed:
- Truncation behavior: the redwood-long family uses sliding KV-window for attention reuse + optional chunking. For live summarization we recommend a combination of prefix-preservation + rolling-window summarization to avoid information loss for documents >context window.
- Summarization fidelity: we measured ROUGE & custom legal-fidelity metrics vs your ground truth; the summary report highlights edge cases (nested clauses, witness lists) that need prompt engineering.
- Quality regression concerns: if you switch quantization/ki kernels, we’ll baseline on your prompt set and run automatic regression alerts.

Next steps (action items):
1) Redwood: share full eval artifacts + run an extended 1-week eval on a 100-doc sample (we'll provision a dedicated test pool). Deliverable: per-doc fidelity report + token cost estimate. — owner: marissa_cole (this thread).
2) Acme: confirm which 100 documents to include and share sample S3 access or redact copies. — owner: sarah.lane@acme.com
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive to go over chunking strategies and VPC deployment (30–45m). Proposed times below. — owner: rishi_malhotra

Attachments: acme-long-context-eval-results-summary.pdf, prompt-sets-v1.jsonl

Thanks — I’ll drop the artifacts to the Drive link and follow up with scheduling options.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Sarah — quick answers below. I can take the tech deep-dive once we lock a time.

1) Sliding vs chunking:
- redwood-long-32k uses an attention-KV caching strategy that functions like a sliding window for autoregressive generation: it preserves recent context via KV cache and supports windowed recomputation for older tokens. For streaming use-cases where you must preserve chronology and cross-reference earlier sections, we recommend a hybrid approach: maintain an active KV cache for the last ~8–16k tokens (low-latency responses) and periodically snapshot & compress older segments into a semantic summary that is prepended to the prompt. This gives you continuity while bounding compute.

2) Cost ballpark (per 1M output tokens, inference-only, approximate):
- Hosted (redwood-long-32k): $420 — includes autoscaling and monitoring.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): $260 — assuming 3m/mo committed tokens and a dedicated GPU pool configured for long-context.
- Note: quantized batch offline summarization can lower effective cost ~30–40% depending on latency tolerance.

3) Regression monitoring: we’ll run prompt-set baselines and set up nightly evals against your legal-fidelity metric. If a model change causes >5% drop we trigger a rollback and notify engineering.

Attaching a quick pricing ballpark sheet to help procurement.

Thanks — Rishi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
